key_insight: AI agents could deepen inequality when people differ in whether they can access agents, how capable those agents are, and how many they can use. This paper offers a conceptual framework for examining these disparities and a research agenda for addressing them.
problem_solved: Clarifies how unequal access to AI agents—and differences in their quality and number—could become sources of societal inequality.
method: Develop a conceptual framework to identify potential sources of agentic inequality.
Examine disparities in access to AI agents, agent quality, and the number of agents available.
Propose a research agenda to investigate and help address the resulting societal challenges.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the paper highlights the importance of evaluating who can access and benefit from agentic systems, not just how well those systems perform. It encourages attention to distributional consequences in research and deployment.
visual_elements: Three-axis diagram showing access, agent quality, and agent quantity as dimensions of inequality.
Side-by-side illustrations of users with no agents, one basic agent, and multiple capable agents.
Conceptual flowchart linking differences in agent resources to potential societal disparities.
Research roadmap connecting identified inequality risks to questions for future investigation.
paper_authors: Matthew Sharp, Omer Bilgin, Iason Gabriel, Lewis Hammond
